method: back-view single-camera VIMO/SMPL 3D reconstruction, ankle ground-projected, compared against real top-view ground-truth CSV positions (nearest-neighbor matched per frame). Camera: one hand-calibrated pose (8 real annotated points, RMS 15.5px, solved via court_detection.py _solve_pose_and_focal) reused across all rallies/matches sharing the same fixed physical camera (confirmed identical framing across BD12 and BD13).
tolerance_rationale: 0.8m chosen as a body-scale tolerance: average adult male arm span ~1.8m, and a badminton player's reconstructed 'position' (foot/ankle) vs. the ground-truth annotation point can reasonably differ by less than half an arm span (~0.9m) given players often have an arm/racket extended -- 0.8m is a slightly conservative fraction of that.
